profilePeriod: Premiership, March 2025–September 2026, with dated earlier monetary principles.
scopeNote: Answers are editorial simulations of documented political principles, not a questionnaire completed by the person. Brazil-specific statements are interpreted in the analogous home-country context. Modern hypothetical technologies require inference.

sources.title: One Canadian Economy Act
sources.evidence: Cabinet designates national-interest projects; exclusive provincial jurisdiction requires written provincial consent. Constitutional Indigenous rights remain recognized.

sources.title: BCAFN criticism of Bill C-5
sources.evidence: First Nations organization criticized accelerated passage, inadequate consultation and excessive cabinet discretion; its objection is evidence of contested consent, not a judicial finding.

sources.title: Canada-Australia joint statement
sources.evidence: Carney endorsed parliamentary democracy, multiculturalism, equality before law and First Nations cultures, with open trade and strategic cooperation.

sources.title: Bail and sentencing reforms become law
sources.evidence: Reverse-onus bail for specified repeat/violent offences and tougher sentencing; provinces retain justice administration responsibilities.

sources.title: Lawful access
sources.evidence: Government seeks expanded lawful-access capability in Bill C-22; describes judicial warrants and differentiated thresholds, rather than unlimited warrantless interception.

sources.title: National Day Against Gun Violence
sources.evidence: Carney backs assault-style firearm compensation, red-flag removal and additional RCMP and border personnel.

sources.title: Controlled immigration increase discussion
sources.evidence: Canadian Press reports Carney considering when controlled population growth can resume after curbing student and temporary-worker admissions; no new target announced.

sources.title: Canadian Multiculturalism Day
sources.evidence: Carney explicitly values bilingual, multicultural Canadian nationhood, cultural and linguistic traditions, and reconciliation.

sources.title: NATO Summit defence partnerships
sources.evidence: Carney supports NATO collective defence, Arctic security, expanded procurement, deterrence and Ukraine, with a path toward the alliance spending commitment.

sources.title: UN General Assembly priorities
sources.evidence: Carney backed UN cooperation and international law, Palestinian humanitarian assistance and two-state diplomacy; government also imposed targeted Iranian human-rights sanctions.

sources.title: Canada Strong Fund
sources.evidence: A public sovereign fund was announced to invest alongside private capital in infrastructure, minerals, agriculture and conventional and clean energy.

sources.title: Canada Investment Summit remarks
sources.evidence: Carney touts tax reductions, regulatory acceleration, private investment and operating restraint while preserving social programs; favors nuclear, resource exports and carbon capture.

sources.title: Lambda, lambda, lambda
sources.evidence: Carney defends operational monetary independence under democratically set objectives and parliamentary accountability; distinguishes delegated expertise from unlimited discretion.

sources.title: China strategic partnership remarks
sources.evidence: Carney announced a quota of 49,000 Chinese EVs at a 6.1% tariff, linking affordable imports to investment and domestic industrial development.

sources.title: Deeper European partnership
sources.evidence: Carney seeks greater EU economic integration and defence cooperation, including critical minerals and technology, as means to strategic autonomy.

sources.title: Faith and service after papal Mass
sources.evidence: Carney says Catholic faith motivates public service but does not determine government policies; he personally participates in Catholic worship.

sources.title: Pride flag ceremony
sources.evidence: Canadian Press reports Carney defending LGBTQ dignity, inclusion and representation, and funding security for Pride festivals.

sources.title: Digital Transformation Canada
sources.evidence: Government promotes responsible AI adoption, digital public services and procurement supporting Canadian technology firms.

sources.title: Ocean protection investment
sources.evidence: Carney links expanded ports and maritime trade to ecosystem protection, monitoring and conservation funding.

sources.title: Value(s), publisher record
sources.evidence: Publisher identifies Mark Carney as author of Value(s): Building a Better World for All, a 2021 political-economic critique of market values and plan for responsible capitalism.

sources.title: Canada Strong platform
sources.evidence: Search-indexed primary platform excerpts support public healthcare expansion and permanent reproductive-health funding. Full PDF fetch failed; claims limited to retrieved excerpts.

sources.title: Carney public-healthcare pledge
sources.evidence: Reporting records Carney defending healthcare as a right and promising public-system expansion in cooperation with provinces and Indigenous peoples.

sources.title: MAID extension deliberation
sources.evidence: Carney deferred a position on extending assisted dying to mental illness alone pending committee evidence; this is separate from established terminal-illness access.

sources.title: Defence Industrial Strategy
sources.evidence: Carney favours Canadian procurement, drone innovation and defence industrial capacity, making strategic protection compatible with exports to allies.

facts: National project approvals coexist with written provincial consent in exclusive jurisdiction (2025).
Justice administration remains provincial (2026).
estrutura.tension: Cooperative federalism and Indigenous rights are constrained by accelerated national projects; Indigenous critics dispute meaningful consultation.

facts: Endorsed parliamentary democracy in March 2026.
Monetary expertise must be democratically delegated and accountable (2017).
representacao.tension: Technocratic executive administration is not support for abolishing elections; project discretion still provokes oversight criticism.

facts: Tougher bail/sentences, expanded policing and gun restrictions in June 2026.
Lawful interception is supported with legal safeguards.
poder.tension: Personal medical choice coexists with coercive public safety; mental-illness MAID extension was explicitly unresolved.

facts: Explicitly celebrates multiple languages and cultures (2025).
September 2026 remarks contemplate controlled increases after intake reductions.
imigracao.tension: Capacity limits and national identity do not imply ethnic assimilation or open borders.

facts: NATO procurement, deterrence and Ukrainian support increased in 2026.
September UN diplomacy supports negotiated peace.
diplomacia.tension: Armed collective security alongside multilateralism; neither absolute pacifism nor preventive conquest.

facts: September 2026 sanctions and international partnerships advance influence.
Supports UN Charter and a two-state settlement.
intervencao.tension: Assertive Canadian sovereignty and alliances coexist with rejection of coercive great-power domination.

facts: Public healthcare remains a commitment.
Sovereign fund co-invests with private businesses; September agenda prioritizes investment and operating restraint.
economia.tension: No blanket nationalization or universal privatization: social services and productive investment have different ownership logics.

facts: 2017 monetary doctrine protects operational independence.
2026 combines tax reductions/regulatory reform with strategic public investment.
controle.tension: Market allocation and independent stabilization coexist with industrial policy; regulation is not comprehensive planning.

facts: January 2026 China EV agreement retains quota and tariff while expanding access.
September EU integration and February domestic procurement favor diversified but secure trade.
comercio.tension: Reject both autarky and unconditional tariff abolition; calibrated openness protects selected domestic capacities.

facts: May 2025 Catholic worship and explicit separation of personal faith from policies.
religiao.tension: Personal faith and service are sincere; secular legislation does not entail hostility to religion or removal of religious tradition.

facts: June 2026 Pride speech endorses LGBTQ equality.
2025 reproductive-health commitment and Catholicism coexist.
moral.tension: Liberal civil rights do not establish strong opinions about every sexual practice or deny families a moral role.

facts: September 2026 AI modernization and industrial energy strategy.
September ocean investment protects ecosystems while supporting infrastructure.
tecnologia.tension: Growth through technology is bounded by environmental and ethical safeguards; no verified advocacy of unrestricted human enhancement.

uncertainties: A modeled response set, not a questionnaire personally completed by Carney. Questions naming Brazil are transferred to analogous Canadian institutions and general policy principles.
Current-date searches conducted on 2026-10-01; preserve explicit source profile period March 2025–September 2026. Announcements establish preferences, not proof of delivery.

No direct personal statements verified for embryo enhancement, brain implants, polyamory, facial recognition, racial quotas as a specific mechanism or Brazilian agrarian reform. Such answers are lower-confidence inferences from stated rights, regulated innovation and property principles; N is reserved for competing considerations.
Platform PDF and party healthcare page failed full fetch; retrieved primary search excerpts plus independent healthcare reporting are identified separately.
